newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short term rates ease further, ecu/drach up.
newsitem.headline: Greek short term rates ease further, ecu/drach up.

text.p: Greek short-term rates were easier in late lacklustre trade with overnight funds trading between 13 and 13.10 percent on an improved liquidity outlook, dealers said.

Ecu/drachma continued its latest upward course at the central bank's fixing at 301.62 from Thursday's 301.480 and forex traders attributed it to the Bank of Greece's desire to drive it higher by year-end.
"Overnight funds trade around 13.00-13.10 percent in late dealings and short term money rates have eased more on an improved liquidity outlook," said a dealer at a foreign bank.

Sales of T-bills on Thursday turned out exceptionally strong traders said as fixed income investors are expecting the government to decide in favour of taxing interest earned on state debt paper in the near future.
The central bank intervened again on both sides of the overnight, draining liquidity at 12.40 percent and injecting cash at 13.40 percent.
And state National Bank announced on Friday it will trim its savings deposit rate by 25 basis points down to 11.25 percent effective on Monday November 4.
The mark was quoted at 157.16/21 drachmas from Friday's 157.025 fix, the dollar at 238.47/57 drachmas from 238.600 and the Ecu at 301.31/36 from 301.620 drachmas.
